PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

minutes_text:
AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called meeting to order at 5:14 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any Closed Session items.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council recessed to Closed Session at 5:15 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council reconvened to open session at 6:10 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session Item No. 1, stating that with the entire Council present, three potential litigation matters were discussed. Staff provided a presentation, the City Council gave direction, and no reportable action was taken.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called meeting to order at 6:11 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Finance Director Castellon led the Pledge of Allegiance. 

INVOCATION Councilmember Rebollo offered the invocation

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Proclamation Declaring September 2025 as Deaf Awareness Month in the City of Commerce Assistant Director of Parks and Recreation Marquez gave a brief presentation on Deaf Awareness. Mayor Altamirano then read the proclamation and presented it to Ruben Aries.


PUBLIC COMMENT Gloria Nezahualcoytl requested that more senior classes be brought back and also asked that shuttle service be provided for the Fiesta Padres event.

Herlinda Chico, LA County Fire Department, spoke about two programs: the CERT class, which is free and also offered in Spanish at the East LA Service Center; and the upcoming Girls Camp on October 4, focused on fire safety. She asked that the event be shared with schools, parent groups, and on social media.




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo

4.. Adoption and Second Reading of an Ordinance Amending Commerce Municipal Code Title 5, Chapter 5.48, Relating to Card Club Pointholders Minimum Interest

2.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 3A, 3B, 3B S/A, 26A, and 26B

5.. Fourth Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with Clean Energy

3.. Updated Library’s Collections Development Policy

SCHEDULED MATTERS

6.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Jimenez provided an overview of the August statistics and reported on the active shooter training that took place at the Citadel Outlets. He expressed his gratitude to the City Council and staff, noting that this was his last meeting, and introduced the new Sergeant, Alvaro Barreras. Mayor Altamirano and the City Council thanked Sergeant Jimenez for his dedication and professionalism.


7.. Committee and Commission Appointments Councilmember Garcia reappointed Jesus Cervantes to the Senior Citizens Commission and appointed Dannielynn Escobar to the Youth Advisory Commission.

8.. Consideration of Creative Crosswalks Artwork and Contract Award This item was continued to a future date. 

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Rebollo reported that she attended the Contract Cities Conference, where Sheriff Luna shared information about a new patrol system involving drones, as well as legislation regarding housing control and its potential impact on the City of Commerce. She also highlighted resources available in the library related to Deaf Awareness. 

Councilmember Garcia expressed her appreciation for the awareness being raised during Deaf Awareness Month. 

Councilmember Argumedo noted that he also attended the Contract Cities Conference, which was well attended. 

Mayor Pro Tem Lainez reminded everyone about the upcoming Fiesta Patrias event.  

Mayor Altamirano announced that the first Paul Botello art piece has been installed at the Mixmaster under the bridge.



ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 6:55 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
